label: <DEL> step in long sequences (L >= 7)
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires at the delimiter step (<DEL> input, first copy output) of sequences with 7 or more original tokens. Here it is active on essentially every such sequence, near max magnitude (precision 1.0, about 95% of activation mass). It almost never fires on L <= 6 (a few L=6 delimiter steps) and never during the original phase. Weak spillover (the low-magnitude bottom quartile) happens on the next step (recall_idx 1, input = first original token), mostly in L >= 8 sequences, and a trace at recall_idx 2. Activation does not depend on token identity (out_tok, first_tok, prev tokens are all flat), so it reads as a length-gated signal for the start of copying.

issues: Each factual claim checks out on test: precision 1.0, F1 0.871, mass recall 0.946, 0 false positives. There are only 5 original-phase activations, and the L=6 delimiter firing is only a trace (376 dev steps).
The misses are a systematic class, not noise. 14,759 test misses (5.4% of mass), and the sampled ones are almost all the step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1).

The explanation says these misses are 'mostly in sequences with L >= 8'. In fact they are concentrated in L = 9. (recall_idx==1)&(L==9) has precision 0.65, while L=8 has 0.18 and L=7 has about 0. The agent only tested the broader L>=8 extension, which pulls precision down to 0.77, and so wrongly decided the misses should be left out.
Adding (recall_idx==1)&(L==9) to the predicate raises test F1 from 0.871 to 0.926 (precision 0.913, recall 0.939, mass recall 0.992).
Minor: by t, t=10 (L=9, recall_idx 1) has a 16.6% active rate, so 'never fires after the delimiter' would be wrong. The label is acceptable because these firings are weak.
skeptic.revised_label: Mainly the <DEL> step in long sequences (L >= 7), plus weak firing on the first copy step after <DEL> when L = 9

final_label: Mainly the <DEL> step in long sequences (L >= 7), plus weak firing on the first copy step after <DEL> when L = 9
